scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: The Connection Lab receives a fictional offer of a free art kit. Below the colourful prize picture, the message asks for a small entry fee and says the offer must be kept secret. Tara reads the requested action before deciding whether the reward matters.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: Neel thinks a small payment might be a harmless way to test the claim. The teacher explains that making the requested payment is already acting on an unverified demand. A short deadline and a secrecy request increase pressure; neither proves that the sender has authority to offer anything.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The team pauses, keeps a minimal record and asks a trusted adult to check through an already known school contact. It does not use a new contact supplied by the same message as independent proof. Learners use pretend tokens only; real purchase decisions belong with responsible adults.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: The unverified message promises a free kit but demands payment and secrecy. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Pause and verify through a trusted adult using a known route. Paying even a small amount would follow the unverified demand rather than independently check it.

scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate promise and demand, then pressure tactics, then independent checking. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
